# Results — Study 613 (Currency-Hedged ETF Carry)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
currency hedge inside a hedged equity ETF mechanically pockets the US-vs-foreign short-rate
differential** ("free carry hidden in a share class") — tested on three live share-class pairs:
**DXJ vs EWJ** (Japan, 2010-04+, different baskets — DXJ only adopted the hedged mandate on
2010-04-01, so its unhedged-dividend era is excluded; on the tape its hedge β is −0.15 before
that date vs +0.94 after), **HEWJ vs EWJ** (Japan, 2014+, the SAME basket — HEWJ literally
holds EWJ plus one-month JPY forwards), and **HEDJ vs VGK** (Europe, 2012-02+, different
baskets — HEDJ likewise sliced from its hedged-mandate start). Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `866b58311fd5`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes: DXJ, EWJ, HEWJ, HEDJ, VGK + spot `JPY=X`, `EURUSD=X` + `^IRX` (13-week T-bill, %) — public, no key |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 daily; **257** complete months in the panel (per-pair windows below) |
| Foreign short rates | **hardcoded policy-rate step tables** in [`data.py`](../currency_hedged_etf_carry/data.py): BOJ uncollateralized overnight call-rate target (boj.or.jp) and ECB deposit facility rate (ecb.europa.eu) — coarse (±~15 bp vs 3M interbank) but the carry story lives at the 1–5 %/yr scale |
| The identity | `hedged − unhedged ≈ carry − fx` ⇒ **carry_hat = (hedged − unhedged) + fx**, where `fx` is the USD return of holding the foreign currency |
| Inference | **Newey-West HAC *t*** (6 lags; sensitivity at 3/12 below) on means and on the OLS of `diff` on `−fx` |
| Execution / costs | share-class **switch** uses the *prior* month-end rate differential (one-month lag, the differential is an observable policy rate); a switch costs 2 × 5 bps one-way; the isolation spread pays **50 bps/yr borrow** on the short leg + 5 bps one-way × ~2 rebalances/yr |

> **Survivorship / selection note.** All five ETFs are live, multi-billion survivors — but the
> *effect* is a per-month arithmetic property of the hedge overlay, not a cross-sectional pick,
> so survivorship bias is minimal here; the honest selection caveat is that these are the
> *flagship* hedged wrappers (the ones that gathered assets), not a random sample of all hedged
> share classes ever launched.

## Full sample — the identity holds, and the clean pair prices it

Regression is `(hedged − unhedged)_t = α + β·(−fx_t)`: **β ≈ 1** means the wrapper really is a
full short of the currency; **α** is the monthly carry (plus basket alpha where baskets differ).

| pair | window | n | β (HAC t) | R² | carry_hat (bps/mo) | carry (%/yr) | HAC *t* | observable rate-diff (%/yr) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DXJ/EWJ (baskets differ) | 2010-04→2026-06 | 195 | 1.050 (+26.8) | 0.779 | +21.08 | **+2.53** | **+2.24** | +1.44 |
| **HEWJ/EWJ (same basket)** | 2014-03→2026-06 | 148 | **0.971 (+28.4)** | **0.868** | **+19.92** | **+2.39** | **+4.54** | +1.89 |
| HEDJ/VGK (baskets differ) | 2012-02→2026-06 | 173 | 0.979 (+17.4) | 0.680 | +8.19 | +0.98 | +0.84 | +1.11 |

The **same-basket pair is the proof**: HEWJ = EWJ + forwards, and its return differential is
β = 0.97 of the (inverted) yen move with R² = 0.87, leaving a carry component of **+2.39 %/yr at
HAC *t* = +4.54** against an observable policy differential of +1.89 %/yr. (The ~0.5 %/yr excess
over the *policy* differential is consistent with the persistently **negative JPY cross-currency
basis** — a USD hedger selling yen forward earns the differential *plus* the basis — plus our
coarse policy-rate proxy.) DXJ corroborates at *t* = +2.24 with β = 1.05 — a full hedge too,
once its window starts at the actual hedged mandate — but its α mixes carry with its
exporter-tilt basket alpha, so the same-basket pair stays the proof. The EUR pair's hedge
mechanics are equally real (β = 0.98) but its average differential was small (+1.11 %/yr) and
basket mismatch noise swamps the mean: *t* = +0.84 — **named on the Signal axis** as the split.

## High-differential era (2022-07 → 2026-06, 48 months; Fed ~5 % vs BOJ ~0)

| pair | carry_hat (bps/mo) | carry (%/yr) | HAC *t* | rate-diff (%/yr) | β | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DXJ/EWJ | +67.05 | +8.05 | +4.75 | +4.20 | 1.047 | 0.805 |
| **HEWJ/EWJ** | **+40.26** | **+4.83** | **+6.01** | **+4.20** | 0.980 | 0.879 |
| HEDJ/VGK | +21.89 | +2.63 | +0.90 | +1.71 | 0.941 | 0.621 |

When the Fed put ~5 % between USD and JPY short rates, the hedged share class pocketed
**+4.83 %/yr** of pure carry (same-basket pair) at **HAC *t* = +6.01** — within ~0.6 pp of the
observable policy differential. Free carry, hidden in a share class, exactly as the claim says.

## Does the pocketed carry TRACK the differential? (12-month rolling)

| pair | corr(rolling carry, rolling rate-diff) | pass-through slope | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| DXJ/EWJ | +0.621 | +1.830 | 184 |
| **HEWJ/EWJ** | **+0.851** | **+0.984** | 137 |
| HEDJ/VGK | +0.227 | +1.066 | 162 |

On the clean pair the rolling carry tracks the observable differential at **corr = 0.85** with a
pass-through slope of **0.98** — one-for-one. The mismatched-basket pairs are noisier: DXJ
tracks at corr 0.62 but its slope overshoots (basket alpha co-moved with the high-differential
era) and the EUR pair's thin differential is buried under basket noise.

## HAC-lag sensitivity — the headline *t* is not a lag artefact

| NW lags | HEWJ/EWJ full-sample *t* | HEWJ/EWJ 2022+ *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 | +4.07 | +4.51 |
| **6 (headline)** | **+4.54** | **+6.01** |
| 12 | +4.15 | +7.67 |

## Tradability — you can actually pocket it

**(a) Zero-extra-cost version — just hold the hedged share class.** ERs (fund pages, 2026):
DXJ 0.48 % ≈ EWJ 0.50 %; **HEWJ 0.50 % = EWJ 0.50 %** — for Japan the wrapper is free. But
**HEDJ 0.58 % vs VGK 0.09 %**: the Europe wrapper charges ~0.5 %/yr, eating roughly half of the
EUR pair's average differential.

**(b) Isolating the carry (long hedged / short unhedged), 2022+ era, net of 50 bps/yr borrow +
5 bps one-way × ~2 rebalances/yr (total charge 0.70 %/yr):**

| pair | raw spread net (%/yr) | HAC *t* | fx-stripped carry net (%/yr) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DXJ/EWJ | +11.05 | +2.74 | +7.35 | +4.34 |
| **HEWJ/EWJ** | +7.84 | +2.19 | **+4.13** | **+5.14** |
| HEDJ/VGK | −0.57 | −0.17 | +1.93 | +0.66 |

*The raw spread is also short the foreign currency (a live FX bet); the fx-stripped column is
the pure pocketed carry after the same charges — **+4.13 %/yr at t = +5.14** on the clean pair.*

**(c) Share-class switch (one-month lag, hold hedged when the prior month-end differential
> 1 %/yr; 2 × 5 bps per switch):**

| pair | switch net (%/yr) | always-hedged (%/yr) | always-unhedged (%/yr) | switches / months |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| DXJ/EWJ | +10.62 | +13.34 | +7.82 | 3 / 195 |
| HEWJ/EWJ | +11.87 | +14.21 | +8.48 | 3 / 148 |
| HEDJ/VGK | +9.02 | +11.26 | +9.57 | 5 / 173 |

The switch rule beats always-unhedged on both Japan pairs at trivial turnover (3–5 switches in
12–16 years). It trails always-hedged *ex post* — because the yen fell for over a decade, a
currency outcome nobody knew ex ante. The switch harvests the **observable** carry without a
permanent FX view; always-hedged bundles the carry **with** a permanent short-yen bet.

## Third axis — when there was NO carry to pocket, was unhedged the better class?

Near-zero-carry era (2010-04 → 2015-12, 69 months; US and JP short rates both pinned at ~0,
mean differential **+0.01 %/yr** — window starts at DXJ's hedged-mandate date), DXJ vs EWJ:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| hedged − unhedged | **+28.32 bps/mo** (t = +0.82) |
| fx (yen USD return) | −33.80 bps/mo |
| **carry component** | **−5.48 bps/mo = −0.66 %/yr (HAC t = −0.49)** |

**Busted.** With nothing to pocket, the carry component was statistically zero — exactly as the
mechanics demand — yet the hedged class *still* beat unhedged, entirely because the yen fell
(Abenomics). At a zero differential the share-class choice is a **pure currency bet**, not a
carry harvest; and "unhedged wins when carry is negative" finds no support because the USD-JPY
differential never went meaningfully negative on this tape and the FX leg dwarfs the carry leg
whenever the differential is thin.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never market evidence)*

Deterministic world (`synthetic_world`, seed 613): hedged = local + planted carry + tracking
noise; unhedged = local + fx + tracking noise.

| planted carry | recovered carry_hat | HAC *t* | β |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 %/yr (null) | +0.15 %/yr | **+0.37** | 0.997 |
| +5 %/yr | **+5.15 %/yr** | +12.68 | 0.997 |

The zero-carry null does not fire; a planted +5 %/yr is recovered at +5.15 %/yr. The estimator
is unbiased — so the real-tape *t* = 4.5–6.0 is the genuine article.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** On the same-basket pair (HEWJ = EWJ + forwards) the hedge is a full
  currency short (β = 0.97, R² = 0.87) and the residual carry is **+2.39 %/yr at HAC
  *t* = +4.54** full-sample, **+4.83 %/yr at *t* = +6.01** in the 2022+ high-differential era —
  tracking the observable policy differential at corr 0.85, slope 0.98, robust to the NW lag
  choice (t = 4.1–7.7). DXJ corroborates (*t* = +2.24 / +4.75, β = 1.05 from its 2010-04
  hedged-mandate start) with exporter-basket alpha mixed
  in. The **EUR pair is the honest split**: mechanics identical (β = 0.98, pass-through slope
  1.07) but its small ~1.1 %/yr average differential can't clear *t* ≥ 2 through
  mismatched-basket noise (*t* = +0.84).
- **Tradability — INVESTABLE.** The Japan wrapper is literally free (HEWJ ER = EWJ ER), one
  click, multi-billion capacity; the fx-stripped isolation trade nets **+4.13 %/yr at
  *t* = +5.14** after borrow + costs in the 2022+ era; the switch rule needs 3–5 trades a
  *decade*. Caveats stated: what you pocket is the **observable, moving differential** (BOJ
  hikes had already shrunk it from ~5.3 % to ~3.3 % by mid-2026 — the tap closes as rates
  converge), and the Europe wrapper's 0.5 %/yr ER gap eats half its average differential.
- **"Unhedged was better when carry was ~zero"? — BUSTED.** In 2010–2015 (differential
  +0.01 %/yr) the carry component was −0.66 %/yr (t = −0.49) — nothing to pocket, as the
  mechanics demand — yet hedged still won +28 bps/mo on the falling yen. At a thin differential
  the share-class choice is a pure FX bet, not a carry decision.
